newsitem.title: UK: UK shares stumble as futures get another battering.
newsitem.headline: UK shares stumble as futures get another battering.

text.p: Britain's FTSE 100 blue-chip index fell on Monday, knocked down by a bearish stampede in the futures market on continued worries about interest rates and the new Labour government's July 2 budget.
Another volatile futures session saw the September contract extend Friday's sharp fall and tumble to a substantial discount to the spot market.

By 1000 GMT the FTSE was down 24.2 points to 4,569.7, clambering back from a low of 4,548.5 as futures cut their early losses. The September FTSE contract was down 34.0 at 4,570.0, having dropped as low as 4,525.0 earlier.
Fair value for the September contract is around 32 points above the spot FTSE, dealers said.

"The futures have been hammered again today and that's pulled the FTSE lower," one dealer said. "It seems the market just can't get over its worries about rates and the Budget and we just keep on going down."

The FTSE has been falling continuously since reaching a new closing high of 4,783.1 on June 13. Dealers blame growing expectations of significant interest rate rises this year, as well as concern about the possible abolition of tax breaks on dividends for pension funds in the July Budget.
"We are now five percent off the high," said the head of trading at one brokerage. "Obviously we are going to be rocked ahead of the Budget but we have come off a long way."

But some analysts said the abolition of dividend tax credit could take 10 percent off the FTSE, giving the index further to fall on top of its losses since last Monday when the market began fretting about the possibility the tax break would be scrapped.
Sterling's ascent to 59-month highs against the German mark was also bearish for currency-sensitive stocks and was further damaging sentiment, dealers said.
Declining stocks in the FTSE outnumbered gainers by four to one.
British Steel was the biggest percentage loser among the blue chips, down 10-3/4p to 147-1/2. The stock went ex-dividend, compounding damage from currency concerns.
B.A.T Industries Plc also tumbled, dropping 24-1/2p to 564-1/2 in the wake of Friday's tobacco settlement in the U.S.
WH Smith Group Plc shares fell 31-1/2p to 380 after the retail group said chief executive Bill Cockburn would leave in October to join British Telecommunications Plc.
National Westminster Bank was the FTSE's strongest performer, climbing 30p to 776-1/2 on press reports that it could be the subject of a bid from rival bank Barclays Plc .

Mining, trading and hotels conglomerate Lonrho Plc climbed 1/2p to 128-1/2 after reporting first-half pre-tax profits of 38 million stg, in line with expectations. The company said it expected good progress this year in hiving off its African trading business.
Halifax Plc and Alliance & Leicester made their FTSE 100 debut, beefing up the already hefty presence of financial stocks in the blue-chip index.
They replaced retailer Burton Group Plc and healthcare and household products group Smith & Nephew Plc .
Both of the FTSE's new entrants were weaker on Monday, with Halifax falling 22p to 748 and A&L 14p weaker at 589.
Dealers said they had been dragged down by the weaker market as well as profit-taking.
-- Andrew Marshall, London newsroom +44 171 542 4026
